JSON branch of action runs applyCompensationNotePatch(compId, rawBody) with no authentication or authorization at all; unauthenticated callers can modify notes on any compensation record by id.
manager_approve/reject only requireRole hr_admin/manager; a manager can approve or reject any compensation record without being the manager-of the employee, and no object-scope predicate is applied.

action only blocks a manager from creating compensation for themselves; employeeId is attacker-controlled, so a manager can create compensation under any employee, including non-direct-reports.

buildCustomRequestDigest spreads attacker JSON criteria over the caller's scope: `{ employeeId: emp.id, ...criteria }` lets a client post employeeId (or $eq filters) to read any employee's HR requests from the full-table dump; no allowlist as in compensation.summary.
loader fetches any onboarding task (plus employee/user) by attacker-chosen task id with no ownership/role check; an employee can read other employees' onboarding task details.

action status update on onboardingTasks.id uses no ownership/role predicate (safe sibling applyOnboardingTaskEdits does), enabling arbitrary task status changes including approved/rejected for tasks not owned by the caller.
action updates onboardingTasks by form-supplied taskId with no ownership or role check; any employee can approve/waive/reject any task (self-approval or cross-employee).
